d: Outside atrium of the temple of Janus, with open side door that leads into the temple itself, and which in its time closes. Sabina with following of Roman Matrons in the midst of numerous People, adorning towards the sky and towards the temple the following:
The Best wishes come out with the following of greetings. The door of the temple is closed. The greeting is gladly joined by shouting with others.
Sabina and her follow-up.
Publius Horace, Sabina.

Vast plain all surrounded by magnificent factories, among which the palace of the Orazi. Take Capena to the bottom, which supposedly leads to the city of Alba, which is seen in the façade located above the hill Albano. Other profane and sacred buildings embellish the rest of the scene. Joint Roman senators of the Orazi. Joint Albani of the Curiazi. Marco Orazio, then Curiazio with 'two Brothers and Suguito, then Orazia with Publio Orazio, Sabina and the two other Orazi. People.
Interior atrium of the palace of the Orazi. Licinius, Publius Horace, Sabina.
Marco Orazio, Licinio, Publio Orazio, Sabina.
Choir of many Senators, Marco Orazio, Licinio, Publius Orazio, Sabina.

Magnificent portico in the palace that introduces to a domestic temple adorned with garlands for the wedding feast of Orazia. Priest of Juno with other Ministers who bring the are, faces, basins for libations etc. etc... Curiazio comes from one side with his Brothers, Friends and Conjoints. From the other Publius Orazio, Sabina, Licinio with their Following. Then to the sound of loving march arose accompanied by some Matron Orazia covered by the flammeo, and is led in the middle of the scene.
Marco Orazio with the other Orazi, all previous Actors.
Sabina, Publius Orazio, Marco Orazio, Curiazio.
Marco Orazio, Curiazio.
Inner atrium of the Orazi Palace. Sabina, Licinio.
Licinius alone.
Curiazio, Orazia who follows him, then the Schiera.

Campo Marzio with a view of the two cities Alba and Roma placed opposite each other side by side, and also leads side by side to Rome. At the opening of this scene are already located in their places Mezio Suffezio, dictator of Alba, and Tullo Ostilio, king of Rome, with their respective Schiere the one opposite to the other. I believe completely useless to indicate precisely which should be the pump with which the fight is preceded and accompanied. Licinio with Publio Orazio are near Tullo.

The Orazi and the Curiazi armed with followers of Roman Senators and Albani. Here begins an amazing military march, while from Rome the Orazi with 'Romans, and pass to the other side; and from Alba the Curiazi with the Albani, and pass from the opposite side.
The Orazi, the Curiazi, Tullo, Mezio, Licinio, Senatori albani e romani, Cavalieri, Littori, Popolo.
Horace, Sabina, the Highest Greetings, Priests, People, all coming out of Rome; the above.
Small and pleasant wood consecrated by Numa to the Muse, with clear water falls etc., so you pass at the entrance of the anthrones of the oracles in the Aventine. Publius Orazio, then Sabina.
Publius Orazio, Licinius, then Marco Orazio and numerous follow-up of Roman Senators.
Marco Orazio alone.
Publius Horace returning, Licinius, Senators.

Dark and deep cavern in the cliffs of the Aventine, where you descend for various steep steps which from the top of the theater to the bottom are winding towards the laterals of the aforementioned cave. At the indicated time the shining temple of Apollo will be opened at the bottom from which the answers of the oracles will have to arise. Curiazio, then Oratia, then Marco Orazio, then Publius Orazio, then all the characters later according to the order with which they are called, warning that everyone enters the summit, and then seen or not seen descend to the bottom.
Outside table of the Massimo Circo with closed door that introduces in the same. Sun that rises. Alban senators, Roman senators, supreme greetings; then Roman Matrons, Littori, People.
Curiazio, Orazia, followed by Roman Matrons, then the Augure.
Horace, Roman Matron.

It opens a vast square of Rome with a long way in the prospect, which lets you see in a distance the entrance to Rome of Marco Orazio, which is led over a triumphal chariot adorned with the remains of the three killed Curiazi, among the acclamations and shouts of the Exulting People for the victory report. The rest of the scene, encased with magnificent factories and numerous spectators of the said triumph, forms a framework task of the amazing feast that the various orders of the Priesthood, Politicians and Militaires draw on to form around the triumphant Marco Orazio. Marco Orazio, Augure sommo, Priests, Auguri, Littori, Vestali, Popolo. Roman senators who surround the chariot and accompany it.
Orazia with the hairs scattered and drawing in extreme desolation; then towards the end of the scene Publius Horace and Sabina with Séguito.
